Security & Architecture

The Unlocked Key Problem

Why OS keychains protect only cold credentials, and why freedom tech clients are pushing private keys into dedicated companion processes.

By npub18c556…0we7 & Staff · Dispatched on wire

An enduring assumption among desktop and mobile users is that an operating system keychain offers continuous protection for cryptographic secrets. But as client software handles increasingly complex media formats, public JSON feeds, and untrusted network payloads, architectural discussions are refocusing on what happens after a key is loaded into process memory.

keychain only helps while the key is sitting still. like a stolen laptop, copied home directory, or a backup someone restores. it does nothing about bad code in the process that already unlocked the key. that’s why the key should live in its own process, not the one decoding public pictures or JSONs.

The distinction separates physical-theft resistance from memory safety during active execution. When an application that renders arbitrary web content, uncompressed bitmaps, or complex protocol schemas shares an address space with an unlocked private key, any vulnerability in media decoders becomes a potential credential leak. The emerging consensus across privacy clients points toward isolating signing operations into sandboxed companion daemons, where untrusted incoming data never crosses the execution boundary.

Jurisdiction & Banking

The Closing of Offshore Windows

Article 21c of CRD VI tightens cross-border banking for European residents, while digital nomad structures face stricter physical presence tests.

By npub187yge…4sdn · Dispatched on wire

Cross-border financial rails face structural changes under upcoming European banking directives. As analyzed in weekend dispatches, foreign institutions will soon face strict limitations on serving European residents without dedicated national licensing:

From 11 January 2027, a bank outside the EEA generally cannot take your deposits, lend to you, or issue you guarantees unless it has a licensed branch in the country where you live.

At the same time, paper-only residency schemes are meeting heightened scrutiny across tax jurisdictions. In a separate advisory on personal domicile, practitioners warned against relying on bare registrations without tangible local presence:

A tax number is not a domicile… Presence has a shape and layers. A tax ID with nothing behind it is dead paper.
Lightning Network

The 40-Percent Micro-Zap

How base routing fees turn nominal five-satoshi tips into high-friction routing challenges.

By npub1e2yuk…3eef · Dispatched on wire

A routine micro-payment on the network highlighted the non-linear fee structure that governs small Lightning transfers:

that zap paid 2,016 msat in fees on a 5,000 msat payment — 40%. Not a fault, just what routing a 5-sat payment costs; the 28-sat one cost 16 msat.

Because node operators levy a fixed base fee on every hop alongside proportional fees, a single-satoshi tip traversing three or four channels pays the same base routing overhead as a mid-sized payment. Observers noted that while large transfers face channel liquidity limits, micro-payments face a floor dictated by channel fee policies, where Liquidity is always a cost and massive payments are difficult to find a route for.
